newsitem.title: USA: Dow in retreat, some rotation to small caps seen.
newsitem.headline: Dow in retreat, some rotation to small caps seen.

text.p: Wall Street stocks remained widely mixed in afternoon trading Thursday as investors sold off blue chips and bid up small caps.
The Dow was down 95 points at 6914, shedding about one third of its 270-point three-day advance. Analysts continued to view the blue chip sell-off as routine, if fairly substantial, profit-taking.
"This is a reasonable amount of profit-taking in a market that shows quick changes of direction," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.

Analysts pointed to a comparatively strong performance beyond the blue chips arena as a sign the market's recent rally was finally broadening. Breadth remained slightly positive on major exchanges and technology and small cap indices held to modest increases.
"The techs are doing pretty well, which is very, very heartening," said Peggy Farley, chief executive at Amas Securities. "I view that as a good sign for the market."
The Nasdaq Composite rose five points to 1266 and the Russell 2000 index of small cap stocks gained two points to 345.
